title_en: Lanzhou Changde Materials Development Department v. Lanzhou Municipal People's Government — dispute over approval of recovery of land use rights
keywords_en: administrative; dispute over land use rights; second instance; High People's Court; Gansu Province; legal person; state organ; Land Administration Law; Gansu Province Implementation Measures for the Land Administration Law; legality of withdrawal of land use rights; whether statute of limitations has expired; whether official reply exceeds authority; reversal; grant of land use rights; contract for joint construction of buildings; official reply on withdrawal of land use rights; land use rights; administrative litigation; statute of limitations
full_text_en:
Lanzhou Changde Materials Development Department v. Lanzhou Municipal People's Government — administrative dispute over withdrawal of land use rights approvals

Plaintiff: Lanzhou Changde Materials Development Department, Gansu Province
Legal Representative: Li Tianrong, Manager of the Development Department
Agent ad litem: Wei Zhongyang, Lawyer of Lanzhou Dongfang Law Office, Gansu Province

Defendant: Lanzhou Municipal People's Government, Gansu Province
Legal Representative: Zhu Zuoyong, Mayor of the Municipality
Agents ad litem: Huang Hanwei, Ma Ying, Officers of Lanzhou Urban Planning and Land Administration Bureau, Gansu Province

The plaintiff, Lanzhou Changde Materials Development Department, Gansu Province (hereinafter referred to as Changde Development Department), instituted an administrative action before the Gansu High People's Court because it was dissatisfied with the two official replies of the Lanzhou Municipal People's Government, Gansu Province (hereinafter referred to as the Municipal Government) regarding the withdrawal of its land use rights and the subsequent transfer of those rights to another party. On March 5, 1999, the Gansu High People's Court ruled that the case should be tried by the Lanzhou Intermediate People's Court, Gansu Province.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The defendant, by its Official Replies Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 42 and No. 43, withdrew the state-owned land use rights that had already been granted to the plaintiff and then transferred them to Hua'ou Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hua'ou Company). These two replies of the defendant are based on unclear facts, erroneous application of laws and regulations, and constitute an ultra vires administrative act. The plaintiff requests the court to annul these two replies and to confirm that the defendant's original Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1995) No. 36, which agreed to grant the land use rights to the plaintiff, remains valid.

Defendant's Defense: The plaintiff did not actually acquire the land use rights to the disputed land. The two replies of 1997 were administrative acts performed by the defendant within its authority and in accordance with the law, upon the plaintiff's application. Moreover, the plaintiff's lawsuit has exceeded the statute of limitations. The court should dismiss the plaintiff's claims.

After trial, the Lanzhou Intermediate People's Court found the following facts:

On September 11, 1995, after applying for project approval, submitting a demolition and resettlement report, and signing a draft "State-Owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract for Urban Towns in Lanzhou" with the Lanzhou Urban Planning and Land Administration Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the Planning Bureau), and paying the land use rights grant deposit of RMB 90,000 and Qingyang Road renovation fee of RMB 42,400 as stipulated in the contract, the plaintiff Changde Development Department obtained the Municipal Government's Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1995) No. 36, titled "Official Reply on Granting State-Owned Land Use Rights to Lanzhou Changde Materials Development Department." This reply approved the grant of the use rights to the state-owned urban land located east of Xiaoshaowai, Chengguan District, Lanzhou, and south of Lanzhou Water Pipe Tobacco Factory, with an area of 1,130.3 square meters, to Changde Development Department for construction of a comprehensive building, with a grant period of 50 years.

After obtaining the Municipal Government's approval to grant the 1,130.3 square meters of state-owned land use rights, the plaintiff Changde Development Department, together with Lanzhou Haiqing Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haiqing Company, which had the same legal representative as Changde Development Department), signed a "Joint Building Construction Contract" and a "Supplementary Contract" with Lanzhou Taisheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Taisheng Company) and the First Development Department of Taisheng Company (which later became an independent legal entity, Lanzhou Hua'ou Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hua'ou Company)). The contracts stipulated that Changde Development Department and Haiqing Company would provide the land, while Taisheng Company and its First Development Department would invest, and the parties would jointly construct the building; Changde Development Department would provide materials, certificates, letters of introduction, and other construction-related procedures, and provide original copies of documents such as land allocation documents (maps) and construction plans after the contract became effective. Taisheng Company would assist Haiqing Company in handling preliminary approval procedures, and the First Development Department would be responsible for all development, construction, and property sales.

On May 15, 1996, the plaintiff Changde Development Department and Haiqing Company signed an agreement with Taisheng Company to terminate the "Joint Building Construction Contract." To resolve economic disputes arising from the performance of the "Joint Building Construction Contract," Haiqing Company filed a civil lawsuit with the Gansu High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the Provincial High Court) on May 18. On May 20, the Provincial High Court issued a civil mediation order, which in its first item determined that the "Joint Building Construction Contract" signed by the parties should be terminated, and in its fourth item determined that Taisheng Company should return eight documents delivered by Haiqing Company by May 28 and return newly generated documents related to this project by June 3. During the performance of the mediation order, Haiqing Company and Taisheng Company reconciled on their own on May 27 and agreed to continue performing the "Joint Building Construction Contract" and the "Supplementary Contract." On May 28, the Provincial High Court presided over the parties in reaching an "Enforcement Settlement Agreement," which confirmed that the "Joint Building Construction Contract" would continue to be performed. On the same day, Changde Development Department, Haiqing Company, and Taisheng Company agreed that Haiqing Company's rights and obligations under the "Joint Building Construction Contract" would be fully transferred to Changde Development Department. On November 19, Taisheng Company, Hua'ou Company, and Changde Development Department also agreed that Taisheng Company's rights and obligations under the "Joint Building Construction Contract" would be enjoyed and borne by Hua'ou Company. From then on, the joint building construction matter was performed by Changde Development Department and Hua'ou Company in accordance with the contract. During the performance of its construction obligations under the contract, Hua'ou Company violated the contract and unilaterally decided to construct an additional five floors on top of the originally planned eight-story building. This led to a dispute over the "Joint Building Construction Contract," and Changde Development Department again filed a civil lawsuit with the Provincial High Court on August 15, 1997.

During the performance of the contract, on January 28, 1997, the plaintiff Changde Development Department submitted a report to the Lanzhou Land Paid Use Office, requesting the transfer of the use rights to the state-owned land at No. 96 Xiaoshaowai to Hua'ou Company. On the same day, Hua'ou Company also submitted a report to the Lanzhou Land Paid Use Office, stating: "Our company, after consultation with Changde Development Department, agrees to transfer the use rights to the state-owned land at No. 96 Xiaoshaowai to our company through the Municipal Government." On June 1 and 16, Changde Development Department sent separate reports to the Planning Bureau, the Lanzhou Land Paid Use Office, and the Lanzhou Housing Authority, titled "Report on Withdrawing Document (1997) Lan Chang Zi No. 6," requesting that the procedures for granting the land to Hua'ou Company be stopped. On October 20, the Planning Bureau signed a "State-Owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract for Urban Towns in Lanzhou" with Hua'ou Company, granting the 1,130.3 square meters of land, for which Changde Development Department had already obtained the use rights, to Hua'ou Company. On the same day, the Planning Bureau also submitted a request to the Municipal Government regarding the withdrawal of Changde Development Department's land use rights and the grant of those rights to Hua'ou Company, through documents Lan Gui Tu Di Zi (1997) No. 121 and No. 122. On October 23, the Municipal Government issued Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 42, titled "Official Reply on Withdrawing the Land Use Rights of Lanzhou Changde Materials Development Department," which stated: In accordance with the relevant provisions of the "Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China" and the "Gansu Province Measures for Implementing the Land Administration Law," the use rights to the state-owned urban land located east of Xiaoshaowai, Chengguan District, Lanzhou, and south of Lanzhou Water Pipe Tobacco Factory, with an area of 1,130.3 square meters, are hereby withdrawn for other arrangements. The original Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1995) No. 36 is simultaneously abolished. On the same day, the Municipal Government also issued Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 43, titled "Official Reply on Granting State-Owned Land Use Rights to Lanzhou Hua'ou Real Estate Development Co., Ltd." On November 24, during the Provincial High Court's trial of the "Joint Building Construction Contract" dispute between Changde Development Department and Hua'ou Company, Hua'ou Company presented Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 43 in court. On December 1, the Municipal Government served Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 42 to Changde Development Department. Dissatisfied with the Municipal Government's replies, Changde Development Department filed this administrative lawsuit with the Provincial High Court on December 2, 1997.

It was further found that the Provincial High Court had, on April 9, 1998, made a first-instance judgment in the "Joint Building Construction Contract" dispute case between the plaintiff Changde Development Department and Hua'ou Company, confirming that in that case, the land use rights grant contract signed between the Planning Bureau and Changde Development Department, the "Joint Building Construction Contract" and its "Supplementary Contract" signed between Changde Development Department and Hua'ou Company, and the "Enforcement Settlement Agreement" reached on May 28, 1996, were all valid; and that the land use rights grant contract subsequently signed between the Planning Bureau and Hua'ou Company was invalid and not confirmed. Hua'ou Company, dissatisfied with this civil judgment of the Provincial High Court, has appealed to the Supreme People's Court.

The Lanzhou Intermediate People's Court held that the defendant Municipal Government's Official Replies Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 42 and No. 43 were made based on the request of the Planning Bureau. The Planning Bureau's request, in turn, was formed based on the plaintiff Changde Development Department's report (1997) Lan Chang Zi No. 6 and Hua'ou Company's report (1997) Lan Hua Fang Zi No. (1). The Municipal Government's grant of state-owned land is an administrative act within its authority and is beyond reproach. Changde Development Department filed the lawsuit the day after receiving the Municipal Government's Official Reply No. 42, which did not exceed the statutory period. Therefore, the Municipal Government's defense based on the statute of limitations cannot stand. Accordingly, the Lanzhou Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on May 12, 1999:

Sustain the defendant Lanzhou Municipal People's Government's Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 42, "Official Reply on Withdrawing the Land Use Rights of Lanzhou Changde Materials Development Department," and Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 43, "Official Reply on Granting State-Owned Land Use Rights to Lanzhou Hua'ou Real Estate Development Co., Ltd."

The plaintiff Changde Development Department, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Gansu High People's Court. Grounds of appeal: The facts found by the trial court already show that the appellee Municipal Government lawfully granted state-owned land use rights to the appellant Changde Development Department in 1995. The report (1997) Lan Chang Zi No. 6, made in the name of the appellant, has now been found to have been forged by individuals from Hua'ou Company, and the appellant has declared its withdrawal and nullification, requesting that the transfer of the appellant's state-owned land use rights to Hua'ou Company be suspended. When the appellant had not committed any act violating land administration laws and regulations, the appellee's withdrawal of the appellant's land use rights had no legal basis. Moreover, the appellee first re-granted the land that had already been granted to the appellant, and then withdrew the land use rights already granted to the appellant. This is a serious illegal administrative act of abuse of power. According to the Administrative Procedure Law, the specific administrative act of the appellee constituting an abuse of power should be annulled. The first-instance judgment sustaining it is very erroneous. The trial court, without examining whether the appellee's official reply withdrawing land use rights was lawful, rashly rendered a judgment sustaining it, which clearly violates the principle of legality review under the Administrative Procedure Law. The appellant requests the appellate court to annul the original judgment, confirm that the state-owned land use rights grant contract signed between the appellee's land administration department and the appellant is valid, confirm that the appellee's Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1995) No. 36, "Official Reply on Granting State-Owned Land Use Rights to Lanzhou Changde Materials Development Department," remains valid; confirm that the state-owned land use rights grant contract signed between the appellee's land administration department and Hua'ou Company is invalid, and order the annulment of Official Replies Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 42 and No. 43, and the revocation of the temporary land use rights certificate Lan Guo Yong (1998) No. 1 that the appellee has issued to Hua'ou Company.

The appellee Municipal Government did not submit a defense.

After trial, the Gansu High People's Court found the following facts:

On June 1 and 16, 1997, the appellant Changde Development Department sent separate reports to the Planning Bureau, the Lanzhou Land Paid Use Office, and the Lanzhou Housing Authority, titled "Report on Withdrawing Document (1997) Lan Chang Zi No. 6," requesting that the procedures for granting the land to Hua'ou Company be stopped. The main content was: The report (1997) Lan Chang Zi No. 6, made in the name of Changde Development Department, was, according to an appraisal by the Lanzhou Municipal Public Security Bureau, forged by individuals from Hua'ou Company. Hua'ou Company had committed a breach of contract in performing the "Joint Building Construction Contract," and therefore the land transfer procedures for Hua'ou Company should be stopped.

In the appellee Municipal Government's Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 43, "Official Reply on Granting State-Owned Land Use Rights to Lanzhou Hua'ou Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.," in addition to approving the grant of the disputed land use rights to Hua'ou Company, it also mentioned that the RMB 90,000 land grant deposit previously paid by the appellant Changde Development Department would be deducted from the grant fee payable by Hua'ou Company for this contract; and that all residents and units to be relocated within and outside the boundaries of the granted plot would be organized for relocation by the municipal relocation management department, with Hua'ou Company responsible for resettlement.

When the Planning Bureau was responsible for serving the appellee Municipal Government's Official Replies Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 42 and No. 43, the Planning Bureau only served Official Reply No. 43 to Hua'ou Company and did not serve it to the appellant Changde Development Department. On November 24, during the Provincial High Court's civil trial of the "Joint Building Construction Contract" dispute case, Hua'ou Company presented Official Reply No. 43 in court, and only then did Changde Development Department learn of this official reply. It immediately raised the objection that the disputed land had been granted to them by the Municipal Government through Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1995) No. 36, and now was being granted to Hua'ou Company through Official Reply No. 43, which constituted a duplicate grant. On December 1, the Planning Bureau served the Municipal Government's Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 42 to Changde Development Department.

On April 6, 1998, the appellee Municipal Government issued a "Temporary State-Owned Land Use Rights Certificate" Lan Guo Yong Zi No. 1 to Hua'ou Company.

Except for the above, the Gansu High People's Court confirmed the other facts found in the first instance.

The Gansu High People's Court held:

On September 11, 1995, after applying for project approval, submitting a demolition and resettlement report, signing a state-owned land use rights grant contract with the local government's land administration department, and paying the land use rights grant deposit of RMB 90,000 and the Qingyang Road renovation fee of RMB 42,400 as stipulated in the contract, the appellant Changde Development Department obtained the appellee Municipal Government's Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1995) No. 36, "Official Reply on Granting State-Owned Land Use Rights to Lanzhou Changde Materials Development Department." At this point, Changde Development Department had lawfully obtained the use rights to the disputed land. After successively obtaining approval documents such as the "Construction Land Planning Permit" and the "Demolition Permit," Changde Development Department completed the demolition tasks, and the building jointly constructed with Hua'ou Company had also been completed. Article 17 of the "Interim Regulations of the People's Republic of China Concerning the Grant and Transfer of the Right to the Use of State-Owned Land in Urban Towns" provides: "Land users shall develop, utilize, and operate the land in accordance with the land use rights grant contract and the requirements of urban planning." "If a land user fails to develop and utilize the land within the time limit and under the conditions stipulated in the contract, the land administration departments of the city or county people's government shall correct the situation and may, depending on the circumstances, give a warning, impose a fine, or even impose the penalty of withdrawing the land use rights without compensation." Changde Development Department did not fall under the circumstances that legally warrant the penalty of withdrawal of land use rights.

After the appellant Changde Development Department had raised the issue that the report (1997) Lan Chang Zi No. 6 was forged by individuals from Hua'ou Company, the appellee Municipal Government, acting on the request of its land administration department, did not conduct verification but nonetheless made Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 42 agreeing to withdraw Changde Development Department's land use rights based on that report. This constitutes unclear facts and insufficient primary evidence.

The appellant Changde Development Department did not fall under the circumstances that legally warrant withdrawal of land use rights. In the appellee Municipal Government's Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 42, regarding the legal basis for withdrawing Changde Development Department's land use rights, it only generally mentioned "in accordance with the relevant provisions of the 'Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China' and the 'Gansu Province Measures for Implementing the Land Administration Law,'" without citing the specific applicable articles. This violates statutory procedures.

Before the appellee Municipal Government withdrew the appellant Changde Development Department's land use rights, the Municipal Government's land administration department had, in fact, already granted the same parcel of land use rights to Hua'ou Company. The content of Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 43 involved the interests of both Hua'ou Company and Changde Development Department, but the Municipal Government has to date not served Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 43 to Changde Development Department. These specific administrative acts all violated statutory procedures.

The appellant Changde Development Department and Hua'ou Company are two independent legal persons, and the law does not grant the appellee Municipal Government the power to dispose of the property of the administrative counterparty. In its Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 43, the Municipal Government decided to deduct the RMB 90,000 land grant deposit paid by Changde Development Department from the land grant fee payable by Hua'ou Company. This constitutes an ultra vires administrative act.

Under the auspices of the Provincial High Court, the "Enforcement Settlement Agreement" reached by Hua'ou Company and the appellant Changde Development Department on May 28, 1996, was based on Changde Development Department providing the land and Hua'ou Company providing funds. When the "Enforcement Settlement Agreement" had already become legally effective, the appellee Municipal Government's withdrawal of Changde Development Department's land use rights, rendering this legal document unenforceable, constitutes interference with judicial power by administrative power.

The facts found in the first-instance judgment are basically clear, but the application of law and the reasoning of the judgment are erroneous. Given that the appellee Municipal Government's Official Replies Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 42 and No. 43 suffer from unclear facts, insufficient primary evidence, violation of statutory procedures, and ultra vires acts, the "Temporary State-Owned Land Use Rights Certificate" issued by the Municipal Government to Hua'ou Company pursuant to these replies also constitutes an improper authorization. Article 54, paragraph 2 of the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China" provides: "A specific administrative act shall be annulled or partially annulled by judgment if it falls under any of the following circumstances, and the defendant may be ordered by judgment to make a new specific administrative act: (1) insufficiency of essential evidence; (2) erroneous application of law or regulations; (3) violation of legal procedure; (4) exceeding of powers; (5) abuse of powers." Article 61, paragraph 2 provides that when hearing an appeal case, if the people's court finds that "the original judgment finds the facts clearly but erroneously applies the law or regulations, it shall amend the judgment according to the law." Accordingly, the Gansu High People's Court rendered the following judgment on August 9, 1999:

1. The first-instance administrative judgment is annulled;
2. The appellee Lanzhou Municipal People's Government's Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 42, "Official Reply on Withdrawing the Land Use Rights of Lanzhou Changde Materials Development Department," is annulled;
3. The appellee Lanzhou Municipal People's Government's Official Reply Lan Zheng Di Zi (1997) No. 43, "Official Reply on Granting State-Owned Land Use Rights to Lanzhou Hua'ou Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.," is annulled.

The case acceptance fees for the first and second instances, totaling RMB 200, shall be borne by the appellee Lanzhou Municipal People's Government.
